summary: Fabrizio Ferrari is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He earned his Laurea at Ca' Foscari University of Venice and a PhD from SOAS, later serving as Professor at the University of Chester and Docente di I fascia at Padua.
Fafang (1904–1951) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu. He served as a Research Fellow in Indian Buddhism at Visva-Bharati University.

Fang-Kuei Li (1902–1987) worked in linguistics, sinology, and tibetology. Educated at Tsinghua, Michigan, and Chicago under Sapir, Bloomfield, and Buck, he held posts at Academia Sinica, Yale, Harvard, the University of Washington, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Faren is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD from Lancaster University by 2008. He served as a teaching consultant at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Farzand Ali Durrani (1933–2003) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at the University of Peshawar, University of the Punjab, and University of London. He served as Professor at the University of Peshawar (attested 1990).
Fausta Nowotny (1903–1991) was an Indology scholar who earned her PhD at the University of Vienna under Erich Frauwallner in 1942. From 1943 to 1951, she worked as a collaborator at Weltmuseum Wien.

Fausto Ghirardini Fumi (1840–1915) worked in linguistics and Indology. After studying under Giuseppe Bardelli and at Pisa, Florence, and Leipzig, he taught at Palermo and became ordinary professor and incaricato of Sanskrit at the University of Genoa in 1890.

Fawad Khan is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Peshawar and Quaid-i-Azam University, and served as Assistant Curator at the Directorate of Archaeology and Museums, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (attested 2022).

Fazun (1902–1980) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who studied under Taixu, Amdo Geshe, and Pabongkhapa Dechen Nyingpo, among others. He directed the Institute of Sino-Tibetan Buddhist Studies and served as president of the Buddhist Academy of China.

Federica Venturi is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She earned her PhD from Indiana University Bloomington in 2013 and served as an associate researcher at the Centre de recherche sur les civilisations de l'Asie orientale in 2021.

Federico Squarcini (b. 1967) specializes in Indology and religious studies. He became a professor at Ca' Foscari University of Venice in 2011 and has held editorial roles with Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies and Marco Polo.

Felix Hartmann (b. 1857) was a linguist who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Göttingen under Jacob Wackernagel. He served as an Oberlehrer at Preußische Hauptkadettenanstalt and later as a docent at Berlin (1906–1935).

Felix Solmsen (1865–1911) was a linguist who studied under Johannes Schmidt, Karl Brugmann, and August Leskien at Berlin and Leipzig. He later served as Privatdozent and extraordinary professor at the University of Bonn.

Feng Youlan (1895–1990) was a philosopher and sinologist who studied at Central China Normal University, Peking University, and Columbia University. He held academic posts at Tsinghua University, the University of Pennsylvania, and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Ferdinand Christian Baur (1792–1860) was a religious studies and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at the Tübinger Stift and the University of Tübingen, where he later held a post from around 1826 until 1860.
Ferdinand Hahn (1846–1910) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the Gossner Mission School in 1865 and became a missionary for the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church in 1869.

Ferdinand Hitzig (1807–1875) was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics who studied under Heinrich Ewald. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1833–1861) and Heidelberg University (~1861–1875).

Ferdinand Justi (1837–1907) was an Iranian, Central Asian, and linguistics scholar. He studied at Marburg and Göttingen under Gildemeister, Benfey, and Ewald, later serving as professor of comparative linguistics and Germanic philology and Rektor at the University of Marburg.

Ferdinand Lessing (1882–1961) was a sinologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under F. W. K. Müller. He held posts at Peking University, Berlin's Ethnological Museum, and UC Berkeley.

Ferdinand Masing (1849–1918) was a linguist who studied at the University of Tartu and the University of Leipzig, where his teachers included August Leskien, Georg Curtius, Heinrich Hübschmann, Hermann Osthoff, and Karl Brugmann.
